candidates.exact_span: Pollutants which create a fire or explosion hazard in the publicly owned treatment works (POTW), including, but not limited to, wastestreams with a closed cup flashpoint of less than 140 degrees Fahrenheit or 60 degrees Centigrade using the test methods specified in 40 CPR 261.21
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a numeric threshold (flashpoint < 140 °F / 60 °C) and a referenced test method; whether this prohibition is treated as an enforceable numeric limit for comparison to reported measurements, and which test method governs, could change limit-applicability and exceedance determinations.

candidates.exact_span: Pollutants which will cause corrosive structural damage to the POTW, but in no case discharges with pH lower than 5.0, unless the works are specifically designed to accommodate such discharges
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a floor pH of 5.0 but conditions it on whether the works are designed to accommodate lower pH; different readings of that design exception change whether pH 5.0 is the operative limit and whether missing or conditional evidence should be classified as unresolved versus not applicable.

candidates.exact_span: Solid or viscous pollutants in amounts which will cause obstruction to the flow in the POTW, resulting in Interference,·
candidates.computation_change_reason: Prohibits discharges based on qualitative causation of obstruction and Interference rather than a fixed numeric cap; interpretation of what quantity or condition satisfies this clause could change whether a numeric compliance comparison is deemed applicable.

candidates.exact_span: Any pollutant, including oxygen demanding pollutants (e.g., BOD), released in a discharge at a flow rate and/or pollutant concentration which will cause Interference with the POTW,·
candidates.computation_change_reason: Links BOD and other oxygen-demanding pollutants to flow and/or concentration thresholds tied to Interference; whether this creates a separate enforceable limit or monitoring trigger for BOD-related parameters could change limit comparisons and whether BOD monitoring is required beyond other permit sections.

candidates.exact_span: Heat in amounts which will inhibit biological activity in the POTW resulting in Interference but in no case heat in such quantities that the temperature at the POTW treatment plant exceeds 40 degrees Centigrade (104 degrees Fahrenheit) unless the Approval Authority, upon request of the POTW, approves alternate temperature limits
candidates.computation_change_reason: Contains both a qualitative interference test and a numeric 40 °C ceiling, with a possible alternate limit approved by the Approval Authority; different interpretations of which test applies, whether an alternate limit is in effect, or whether temperature data are adequate could change limit selection and missing-evidence classification.

candidates.exact_span: Petroleum oil, non-biodegradable cutting oil, or products of mineral oil origin in amounts that will cause interference or pass through
candidates.computation_change_reason: Prohibits oil discharges based on interference or pass through rather than a stated numeric concentration; interpretation of those terms and of what constitutes a violating amount could change whether numeric limit comparison is possible or applicability remains unresolved.

candidates.locator: Page 21, Section part_i, F.1 (trucked or hauled pollutants)
candidates.exact_span: Any trucked or hauled pollutants, except at discharge points designated by the POTW.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Restricts hauled discharges to POTW-designated points; whether a given discharge route or period falls inside or outside that exception affects which monitoring and reporting obligations attach and how missing evidence for non-designated haul discharges should be classified.

candidates.locator: Page 21, Section part_i, F.2 (indirect discharger reporting)
candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall require any indirect discharger to the treatment works to comply with the reporting requirements of Sections 204(b), 307, and 308 of the Act, including any requirements established under 40 CPR Part 403.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Imposes permittee-level duties to enforce federal pretreatment reporting requirements; interpretation of which Part 403 reporting obligations are incorporated and for which indirect dischargers could change which monitoring/reporting requirements are deemed applicable in FY2025.

candidates.locator: Page 21, Section part_i, F.3 (notice of new pollutants)
candidates.exact_span: Any new introduction of pollutants into the treatment works from an indirect discharger which would be subject to Sections 301 and 306 of the Act If it were directly discharging those pollutants,·
candidates.computation_change_reason: Triggers permittee notice when new indirect pollutant introductions would have been subject to direct discharge standards; interpretation of what counts as a new introduction and which pollutants meet the Section 301/306 hypothetical-direct test could change whether notice—and any associated monitoring expectations—were required for a given period.

candidates.locator: Page 21, Section part_i, F.3 (notice of substantial change)
candidates.exact_span: Any substantial change in the volume or character of pollutants being introduced into the treatment works by a source introducing pollutants into the treatment works at the time of issuance of the permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Requires notice for substantial changes relative to sources existing at permit issuance; undefined thresholds for substantial change and the baseline at issuance could change whether notice obligations—and downstream monitoring or evidence expectations—were triggered, and whether absent records reflect conditional non-requirement or unresolved missing evidence.

candidates.locator: Page 21, Section part_i, F.3 (adequate notice duty)
candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall provide adequate notice of the following:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a permittee notice obligation whose scope depends on the listed triggers; whether adequate notice constitutes a monitoring or reporting requirement for compliance tracking could change which obligations are counted as applicable in FY2025.
